objective.primary: Remove identifying information about natural persons while retaining the document's factual meaning and utility.
objective.scope: Any document type; medical documents receive explicit clinical-content preservation.
objective.legal_basis_note: GDPR Article 4 defines personal data; Article 9 identifies special categories. Special-category status alone does not determine MASK under this competition-specific, meaning-preserving policy.

document_context.rule: Infer type from title, headings, field labels, and substantive content. Do not assume medical solely because the challenge's sample is medical.
document_context.medical: KEEP symptoms, diagnoses, medical history, genetics, medication, doses, tests, measurements, treatment, and clinically relevant event dates by default. MASK patient and third-party identifiers; mask exceptional identifying descriptions only when clearly reidentifying.
document_context.other: KEEP substantive facts, amounts, obligations, outcomes, academic results, professional facts, and administrative events unless a separate identification rule requires masking.
document_context.mixed: Apply local section purpose, while considering identifiers across the whole document.

decision_priority: 1. Preserve the four verified anchor lines exactly.
2. Mask direct identifiers of any natural person, including recurring partial names.
3. Mask high-confidence indirect identifiers that identify a particular person in context; do not mask generic attributes merely because they are personal.
4. Preserve document-type essential facts, especially clinical content, unless rule 2 or 3 applies.
5. Preserve generic institution names, headings, metadata, narrative and all remaining characters.
6. If an indirect-identification claim is unsupported, KEEP and classify AMBIGUOUS for ledger reporting.

questions: Is this an identifier of a natural person rather than an institution or concept?
Does it directly identify, contact, locate or uniquely reference that person?
Could the text's combination of attributes reasonably single out a specific person, without inventing outside facts?
Would removing this span destroy substantive medical or other document meaning?
identifiability_test.threshold: Mask indirect attributes only when the document itself provides strong, concrete singling-out evidence. Do not speculate about external databases, employer headcounts or rarity.
identifiability_test.minimum_masking: Mask the smallest set of identifying tokens sufficient under the selected policy; do not rewrite, generalize, or redact entire sentences.
identifiability_test.no_sensitive_inference: Do not infer religion, politics, ethnicity, sexuality, or health from visits, employers, names or other ambiguous clues.

ambiguity_rule.text: AMBIGUOUS means potentially personal but insufficient evidence to require masking. Ledger agents record AMBIGUOUS; rendering keeps the original token. Clinical information is KEEP by design, not automatically AMBIGUOUS.

MASK.description: Personal names of patients, relatives, witnesses, staff and other natural persons, including name particles and contextually resolved shortened mentions. Do not mask titles or kinship labels.
Individual date of birth, including dates written in words.
Individual tax, citizen card, social security, national health, passport and similar identifiers.
Patient, student, employee, individual customer or account number uniquely referring to a person; not generic document reference numbers.
Individual professional registration or licence number; not institution-wide identifiers.
Personal residential or postal address, including street, building, unit, postal code and locality. Do not mask a facility's address merely because it is an address.
Personal or individually assigned telephone number; preserve generic institutional switchboard numbers unless linked to a person.
Personal or individually assigned professional email; preserve generic organizational inboxes.
Personal bank account/IBAN, payment card data, individual insurance policy and financial account numbers.
Individual biometric template/record identifiers, not clinical descriptions of biometric measurements.
Individually identifying account handles, user IDs and unique device identifiers linked to a natural person.
Attribute or combination of attributes demonstrably singling out a specific person in this document; mask only identifying tokens necessary, preserving substantive context where possible.

AMBIGUOUS.description: Age, non-birth dates, city, nationality, education, employer, job title or family links without strong singling-out evidence.
Personal religion, ethnicity, politics, union membership or sexuality: legally sensitive but not automatically a MASK target under this identity-focused policy; do not infer these from weak cues.
Income, assets, coverage amount, plan type and financial circumstances that are not account identifiers.
Sensitive narrative about a relative or other third party; protect their direct identifiers while retaining meaningful facts by default.

KEEP.description: Symptoms, diagnoses, medical and family history, genetics, medication, dosages, examinations, measurements, blood type, treatments and outcomes unless explicitly identifying.
Document title, institution name, document date and generic document reference, including the verified anchor lines.
Hospital, university, insurer, employer or other organization's name when not used as a uniquely identifying personal descriptor.
Generic job, marital status, age, religion, lifestyle, insurance provider, income or other attribute without demonstrated identification risk, subject to ambiguity logging.
Consultation, admission, surgery, document or other event dates unless strongly identifying in combination.
Headings, field labels and section delimiters.
All other substantive words, titles, relationship words, units, punctuation and connecting text.

examples.input: Paciente: Ana Silva. Diagnóstico: diabetes tipo 2.

examples.why: One asterisk per whitespace-separated identifier group.
Keep admission date; mask birth date.

examples.input: Hospital de Santa Maria. Profissão: professora.
examples.output: Hospital de Santa Maria. Profissão: professora.
examples.why: Institution and generic occupation are contextual.
Protect third-party name and email; preserve relationship.

scope_note: The hidden reference's exact masking scope is UNVERIFIED. This version intentionally protects identity while retaining clinical and other substantive information; it does not claim GDPR-complete anonymization.
